subject: Creativity
title: The Attention Economy: Creativity's New Battlefield
description: A 60-second lesson on The Attention Economy: Creativity's New Battlefield.

hook.text: You see 6,000+ ads per day. Attention is the scarcest resource in modern economics — and creativity competes for it.

buildup.text: Herbert Simon predicted it in 1971: 'A wealth of information creates a poverty of attention.'

discovery.text: Average human attention span for digital content: 8 seconds.

twist.text: Netflix's biggest competitor isn't Disney+. It's sleep. Every creative product fights for the same scarce attention.

climax.text: The winners aren't the most talented — they understand attention as a currency and craft for retention.

punchline.text: In a world of infinite content, the real creative skill is earning attention.

quiz.question: Who predicted that information wealth would create attention poverty?
